### 2. workspace-infra-resource-cleanup-hygiene

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/GatedCommandExecutor.cs:21` — `_workspaceCommandGates` (`ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim>`) is populated via `GetOrAdd` in `ExecuteAsync` (line 55) but never pruned per-workspace; only `Dispose()` (lines 118-126) clears it. `GatedCommandExecutor` is registered `AddSingleton` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:31`), so every distinct workspaceId ever seen accumulates a permanent `SemaphoreSlim` entry for the process lifetime — unbounded growth across repeated `workspace_load`/`workspace_close` cycles (sweep worktree churn, LRU eviction). `IWorkspaceManager` already exposes a `WorkspaceClosed` event (`WorkspaceManager.cs:94`), raised from both explicit `Close()` (line 398) AND the internal LRU-eviction branch (`Close(lruCandidate.WorkspaceId)` at line 260) — five existing services (`ChangeTracker.cs:21,25,30`, `NuGetDependencyService.cs:57`, `DiRegistrationService.cs:92`, `DiagnosticService.cs:52`, `UndoService.cs:47,56`, `CompilationCache.cs:41,52`) already subscribe to it to prune their own per-workspace state on close/eviction. `GatedCommandExecutor` already injects `IWorkspaceManager` in its constructor (lines 27-32) but never wires the event — that is the gap and the fix mirrors the established pattern exactly. (2) `PersistentCompositeStorage.cs:64` — `TryRead`'s `foreach (var subdir in Directory.EnumerateDirectories(_rootDirectory))` is guarded only by a pre-loop `Directory.Exists` check at line 63 (a TOCTOU window). The class's own stated purpose is cross-process token redemption (`PersistentCompositeStorage.cs:9-11`: "a preview created in one process redeemed by another"), so a sibling process's concurrent `Delete(token)` (lines 100-108) or directory-level cleanup racing the enumeration is a real, not hypothetical, scenario for this multi-agent-orchestration feature. A deletion mid-walk throws `DirectoryNotFoundException`/`IOException` uncaught — the existing try/catch (lines 77-95) only wraps the per-file JSON read, not the enumeration itself. |
| Approach | `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/GatedCommandExecutor.cs`: subscribe to `_workspaceManager.WorkspaceClosed` in the constructor via a named handler (mirrors `ChangeTracker.cs:21,25,30`): add `private void RemoveWorkspaceGate(string workspaceId) => _workspaceCommandGates.TryRemove(workspaceId, out _);`, wire `_workspaceManager.WorkspaceClosed += RemoveWorkspaceGate;` in the constructor, and `_workspaceManager.WorkspaceClosed -= RemoveWorkspaceGate;` in the existing `Dispose()`. Deliberately `TryRemove` WITHOUT calling `.Dispose()` on the removed `SemaphoreSlim`: `SemaphoreSlim.Dispose()` is documented as unsafe to call concurrently with an in-flight `WaitAsync`/`Release()`, and `ExecuteAsync` (lines 55-93) can legitimately be mid-flight against the very semaphore being pruned — the workspace-lifecycle gate (`WorkspaceExecutionGate`) and the command-execution gate (`GatedCommandExecutor`) are two independent locking systems, so a close for workspace X does not guarantee no in-flight `dotnet build`/`test` command for X. Removing the dictionary entry alone satisfies the bounded-growth acceptance criterion; the orphaned semaphore is GC'd once the in-flight caller's local reference (`workspaceGate`, line 55) goes out of scope. The existing `Dispose()` still disposes whatever remains in the dictionary at process shutdown, unchanged. `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/PersistentCompositeStorage.cs`: widen `TryRead`'s try/catch to also wrap the `Directory.EnumerateDirectories` walk (not just the per-file read), catching `IOException` (the shared base of `DirectoryNotFoundException`/`FileNotFoundException`) in addition to the existing generic `Exception` catch, and treating a caught race as a miss (skip to next subdir / return null) — mirroring the file's own existing "corrupt entry — drop it, log at Debug" convention at lines 89-95. |
| Scope | 2 production files: `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/GatedCommandExecutor.cs`, `src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/PersistentCompositeStorage.cs`. 2 test files (both new): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/Services/GatedCommandExecutorTests.cs`, `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/Services/PersistentCompositeStorageTests.cs`. No Rule 3 exemption needed (2 ≤ 4 default cap). |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 38000 |
| Risks | No existing test today asserts anything about `_workspaceCommandGates` retention, so the change is additive-safe. The removed-semaphore-not-disposed design is a deliberate correctness tradeoff (avoids the documented `SemaphoreSlim.Dispose()` concurrent-use hazard) — it satisfies the acceptance criterion's "bounded dictionary size" bar but a strict "dispose every removed semaphore immediately" reading of the row would need a reference-counting wrapper; per Directive #6 (smallest complete fix), that gold-plating is out of scope unless the reviewer explicitly wants it. Widening `PersistentCompositeStorage.TryRead`'s catch to `IOException` could in principle mask a genuinely broken persist directory (e.g. permissions) as a plain cache miss — this matches the file's existing best-effort-persistence philosophy (the in-memory `CompositePreviewStore` is the source of truth; disk is redemption-across-process convenience only), so it is judged consistent rather than a new risk class. Fanout probe was skipped (see Validation/Approach) — this is a targeted 2-file gap fix with no rename/signature-change/cross-cutting symbol edit, so the B1 trigger conditions do not apply. |
| Validation | New test 1 (`GatedCommandExecutorTests.cs`): drive a repeated `workspace_load`→`workspace_close` cycle (e.g. 5 distinct workspaceIds) against a `GatedCommandExecutor` wired to a fake/stub `IWorkspaceManager` that raises `WorkspaceClosed`, calling `ExecuteAsync` once per workspaceId before closing it, then assert the internal `_workspaceCommandGates` dictionary count stays bounded (e.g. via `InternalsVisibleTo` or a reflection-based count helper) instead of growing to 5. New test 2 (`PersistentCompositeStorageTests.cs`): exercise `TryRead` racing a concurrent directory deletion (delete the root/version subdirectory from a background `Task` with a short delay while `TryRead` is enumerating) and assert it returns `null` rather than throwing. Both: `mcp__roslyn__compile_check` after edits; `mcp__roslyn__test_run --filter "GatedCommandExecutorTests|PersistentCompositeStorageTests"` per the repo addenda's per-edit tool primer; fall back to `dotnet build RoslynMcp.slnx -c Release -p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` + `dotnet test --filter` if the MCP tools are unavailable. |
| Performance review | N/A — correctness/resource-hygiene fix, no hot-path behavior change. The `WorkspaceClosed` handler is an O(1) dictionary removal fired once per close/eviction; the widened try/catch in `TryRead` adds no cost on the non-exceptional path. |
| CHANGELOG category | Fixed |
| CHANGELOG entry (draft) | Fixed: `GatedCommandExecutor` now prunes its per-workspace command-execution semaphore on `workspace_close` (including LRU eviction), preventing unbounded growth across repeated load/close cycles. `PersistentCompositeStorage.TryRead` no longer throws uncaught when a preview-token subdirectory is deleted concurrently by another process; the race is now treated as a cache miss. |

### 4. refactor-services-non-atomic-write-rollback

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `CompositeApplyOrchestrator.ApplyCompositeAsync` (`src/RoslynMcp.Roslyn/Services/CompositeApplyOrchestrator.cs:57-89`) writes each queued mutation directly via `File.WriteAllTextAsync` (line 76) with no atomic temp+rename guard — a crash or disk-full condition mid-write can leave a target file truncated/corrupt. This repo already has the correct pattern elsewhere: `PersistentCompositeStorage.Write` (`PersistentCompositeStorage.cs:41-57`) and `WorkspaceCacheStore`'s entry writer (temp-file + `File.Move(overwrite:true)`, confirmed at `WorkspaceCacheStore.cs:164-183`) — but there's no *shared* atomic-write primitive for the source-file mutation paths. The same non-atomic pattern repeats in `EditService.PersistDocumentTextToDiskAsync` (`EditService.cs:664`), `UndoService`'s file-snapshot restore loop (`UndoService.cs:296`) and its `PersistRevertChangesAsync` disk-restore loop (`UndoService.cs:491`, a second write site in the same file the row's Anchors didn't separately enumerate but which shares the identical gap), and `ProjectMutationService`'s `.csproj` write (`ProjectMutationService.cs:562`). ### 5. paramvalidation-pagination-upper-bound-clamp

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | `ParameterValidation.ValidatePagination(int offset, int limit)` at `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ParameterValidation.cs:50-57` only rejects `offset < 0` and `limit <= 0` — there is no upper bound, so a caller (or a malicious/careless LLM tool-caller) can pass `limit: int.MaxValue` and force an unbounded materialization downstream. All 15 call sites across `AdvancedAnalysisTools.cs`, `AnalyzerInfoTools.cs`, `AnalysisTools.cs`, `CompileCheckTools.cs`, and `SymbolTools.cs` route through this single shared validator with the unchanged `(int offset, int limit)` signature, so a cap added here applies uniformly without touching those files. Confirmed via `Grep` there is no existing `int.MaxValue`-as-sentinel usage anywhere in `src/` or `tests/`, so a hard ceiling is safe to introduce without breaking an "unbounded means all" convention. Sibling/dependent row `analysis-tools-pagination-clamp-rollout` (deps: this row) is scoped separately to wire pagination onto tools that currently skip `ValidatePagination` entirely (`find_references_bulk`, `find_consumers`) — that is a distinct code path (missing calls, not an unbounded existing call) and is intentionally NOT bundled here per Rule 1 condition 1 (different symptom, different files: `ConsumerAnalysisTools.cs` isn't touched by this initiative at all). |
| Approach | Single-file change in `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Tools/ParameterValidation.cs`: add a `private const int MaxLimit = 1000;` alongside the existing `*Values` constants, then extend `ValidatePagination` to throw `ArgumentException` when `limit > MaxLimit` (mirroring the existing `ArgumentException`-per-invalid-value style used by `ValidateSeverity`/`ValidateTypeKind` in the same file). No signature change — keeps all 15 existing call sites compiling unchanged, satisfying the item's own acceptance criterion. `MaxLimit = 1000` was chosen because the highest observed default/explicit-clamp in the tool surface today is `500` (semantic_grep's default `limit=500`, and the AdvancedAnalysisTools override-chain summary already self-clamps to `[1, 500]`), so 1000 gives headroom above every current default without being so permissive it defeats the purpose. |

### 6. solutiondiscoveryhelper-hotpath-perf

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis | Three distinct perf smells on the read-only tool-dispatch hot path, all confirmed live in current source: (1) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/SolutionDiscoveryHelper.cs:169-201` `ScanDirectoriesForSolutions` performs synchronous `Directory.EnumerateFiles`/`Directory.EnumerateDirectories` over every declared client root plus one level down, on every read-only dispatch that omits `workspaceId` with zero workspaces loaded — no memoization, so a burst of such calls re-walks the same tree repeatedly. (2) `SolutionDiscoveryHelper.cs:104-125` `TryDiscoverFromFilePath` walks up the directory tree from the call's `filePath` argument to the filesystem root (or nearest `.slnx`/`.sln`/`.csproj`), doing synchronous `Directory.Exists`/`Directory.EnumerateFiles` at every level with no depth cap — worst case is a full ancestor walk on every such call. (3) `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/StructuredCallToolFilter.cs:466-499` — `IsWorkspaceIdRecoveryAllowedFor` (line 466-467) and `IsWorkspaceIdAutoResolveAllowedFor` (line 497-499) both call `ServerSurfaceCatalog.Tools.FirstOrDefault(entry => string.Equals(entry.Name, toolName, ...))` — an O(n) linear scan of the full tool catalog (currently 45 references per `find_references` probe on `ServerSurfaceCatalog.Tools`) executed on every pre-dispatch/exception-path resolution for every read-only tool call. `ServerSurfaceCatalog.Tools` (`ServerSurfaceCatalog.cs:29-32`) is a `Lazy<IReadOnlyList<SurfaceEntry>>` built once at startup and never mutated, so a name-keyed dictionary index is safe and trivial to add — confirmed via `find_references` that only the two `FirstOrDefault` call sites above do this scan pattern; the other 43 references are catalog-partial contributors or existing readers (`PageEntries`, `CountByTier`, `DiffEntries`, three test files) unaffected by adding a parallel index. Not a Rule-1 bundle candidate (bundleCandidatePeers empty). |
| Approach | (1) In `SolutionDiscoveryHelper.cs`, add a short-TTL (~10s) process-lifetime cache keyed by the sorted, ordinal-case-insensitive-joined root-directory list around the call site in `TryDiscoverFromRootsAsync` (not inside the pure, test-covered `ScanDirectoriesForSolutions` itself) — e.g. a `static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, (DiscoveryResult Result, DateTime ExpiresUtc)>` guard so a burst of workspaceId-omitted dispatches within the TTL window reuses the last scan instead of re-walking every root. (2) Add a bounded walk-up depth cap (mirroring the existing bounded one-level-down pattern in `ScanDirectoriesForSolutions`) to `TryDiscoverFromFilePath`'s `while` loop — e.g. cap at 8 ancestor levels — and move the call inside `Task.Run(...)` at its single call site in `TryDiscoverAsync` so the synchronous directory I/O doesn't block the calling async continuation's thread; .NET has no true async `Directory` API so `Task.Run` off-loading plus the iteration cap is the correct "off the hot synchronous path" fix (the acceptance criterion's stated alternative to full async). (3) In `ServerSurfaceCatalog.cs`, add `private static readonly Lazy<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, SurfaceEntry>> s_toolsByName` built once from `Tools` via `ToDictionary(t => t.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal)`, exposed as `internal static bool TryGetTool(string name, out SurfaceEntry entry)`. Update `StructuredCallToolFilter.cs:466-467` and `:497-499` to call `ServerSurfaceCatalog.TryGetTool(toolName, out var tool)` instead of `.FirstOrDefault(...)`, preserving identical `tool is { ReadOnly: true, Destructive: false }` semantics. |
| Scope | 3 production files: `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/SolutionDiscoveryHelper.cs` (cache + depth cap), `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Middleware/StructuredCallToolFilter.cs` (switch two lookups to `TryGetTool`), `src/RoslynMcp.Host.Stdio/Catalog/ServerSurfaceCatalog.cs` (add name-keyed dictionary index). Within Rule 3's 4-file cap, no exemption needed. 2 test files extended (not new): `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/SolutionDiscoveryHelperTests.cs` (cache-hit-within-TTL + depth-cap regression cases) and `tests/RoslynMcp.Tests/StructuredCallToolFilterResolutionTests.cs` (unchanged-behavior regression for `IsWorkspaceIdAutoResolveAllowedFor`/`IsWorkspaceIdRecoveryAllowedFor` post-switch to `TryGetTool`, plus an unknown-tool-name case). Within Rule 4's 3-test-file cap. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 42000 |
| Risks | (1) The TTL cache on `ScanDirectoriesForSolutions`'s callers introduces a staleness window — a solution file created inside the TTL after a cache miss won't be discovered until expiry; keep the TTL short (~10s) and scoped to the no-workspace-loaded cold path only, where staleness is low-stakes (the caller falls back to binder/elicitation regardless).
